```{r}
# ============================================================
# WORLD CASTLES DATASET: EXPLORATORY DATA ANALYSIS (EDA)
# ============================================================


# ============================================================
# SETUP: LOAD PACKAGES AND DATA
# ============================================================

# Run once if tidyverse is not installed:
# install.packages("tidyverse")

library(tidyverse)

world_castles <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-09-01/world_castles.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))


# ============================================================
# EDA 1: DATA STRUCTURE, MISSING VALUES, AND DUPLICATE IDs
# Question: What does the dataset contain, and is anything missing?
# ============================================================

dim(world_castles)
names(world_castles)
glimpse(world_castles)
summary(world_castles)

# Count missing values in each column
missing_table <- world_castles %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "missing_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    missing_percent = round(
      100 * missing_count / nrow(world_castles), 2
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_count))

print(missing_table)

# Check for repeated landmark IDs
duplicate_ids <- world_castles %>%
  filter(!is.na(qid)) %>%
  count(qid, sort = TRUE) %>%
  filter(n > 1)

print(duplicate_ids)


# ============================================================
# EDA 2: FREQUENCY TABLE AND BAR CHART
# Question: Which landmark type is most common?
# ============================================================

category_counts <- world_castles %>%
  filter(!is.na(category)) %>%
  count(category, sort = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

print(category_counts)

p2 <- ggplot(
  category_counts,
  aes(x = reorder(category, n), y = n)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Landmarks by Type",
    x = "Landmark type",
    y = "Number recorded"
  )

print(p2)

# Interpretation:
# The longest bar represents the most common landmark type.


# ============================================================
# EDA 3: RANKED BAR CHART
# Question: Which countries have the most recorded castles?
# ============================================================

country_castles <- world_castles %>%
  filter(category == "castle", !is.na(country)) %>%
  count(country, sort = TRUE)

top10_castles <- country_castles %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

print(top10_castles)

p3 <- ggplot(
  top10_castles,
  aes(x = reorder(country, n), y = n)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkcyan") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Countries by Recorded Castle Count",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Number of castles"
  )

print(p3)

# Interpretation:
# This counts only records classified as castles.
# It does not include palaces, fortresses, or ruins.


# ============================================================
# EDA 4: NUMERICAL SUMMARIES AND HISTOGRAM
# Question: When were landmarks founded?
# ============================================================

dated_landmarks <- world_castles %>%
  filter(!is.na(year))

year_summary <- dated_landmarks %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    earliest_year = min(year),
    Q1 = quantile(year, 0.25),
    median_year = median(year),
    mean_year = mean(year),
    Q3 = quantile(year, 0.75),
    latest_year = max(year),
    SD_year = sd(year)
  )

print(year_summary)

p4 <- ggplot(dated_landmarks, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 100,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Landmark Founding Years",
    subtitle = "100-year intervals; negative years indicate BC",
    x = "Founding year",
    y = "Number of landmarks"
  )

print(p4)

# Interpretation:
# Taller bars show intervals containing more founding dates.
# These intervals are not necessarily named historical centuries.


# ============================================================
# EDA 5: GROUP SUMMARIES AND BOXPLOTS
# Question: Are palaces newer than fortresses?
# ============================================================

palace_fortress <- world_castles %>%
  filter(
    category %in% c("palace", "fortress"),
    !is.na(year)
  )

type_year_summary <- palace_fortress %>%
  group_by(category) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_year = mean(year),
    median_year = median(year),
    SD_year = sd(year),
    IQR_year = IQR(year),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(type_year_summary)

p5 <- ggplot(
  palace_fortress,
  aes(x = category, y = year, fill = category)
) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.75) +
  labs(
    title = "Founding Years: Palaces and Fortresses",
    x = "Landmark type",
    y = "Founding year"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p5)

# Interpretation:
# A higher median founding year means the typical landmark is newer.
# Boxplots alone do not establish statistical significance.


# ============================================================
# EDA 6: GROUPED BAR CHART BY CENTURY
# Question: How do castle and palace counts vary by century?
# ============================================================

# Arrange century labels chronologically using founding years
century_order <- world_castles %>%
  filter(!is.na(century), !is.na(year)) %>%
  group_by(century) %>%
  summarise(first_year = min(year), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(first_year) %>%
  pull(century)

century_counts <- world_castles %>%
  filter(
    category %in% c("castle", "palace"),
    !is.na(century),
    century %in% century_order
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    century = factor(century, levels = century_order)
  ) %>%
  count(century, category)

print(century_counts)

p6 <- ggplot(
  century_counts,
  aes(x = century, y = n, fill = category)
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Castles and Palaces Founded by Century",
    x = "Century",
    y = "Number recorded",
    fill = "Landmark type"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1)
  )

print(p6)

# Interpretation:
# Compare castle and palace counts within each century.
# Look for differences in when their recorded counts peak.


# ============================================================
# EDA 7: PROPORTIONAL STACKED BAR CHART
# Question: Does landmark composition differ by country?
# ============================================================

# Select countries with the most classified landmarks
top_countries <- world_castles %>%
  filter(!is.na(country), !is.na(category)) %>%
  count(country, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  pull(country)

country_types <- world_castles %>%
  filter(
    country %in% top_countries,
    !is.na(category)
  ) %>%
  count(country, category) %>%
  mutate(
    country = factor(country, levels = rev(top_countries))
  )

# Display counts and percentages within each country
country_percentages <- country_types %>%
  group_by(country) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(country_percentages)

p7 <- ggplot(
  country_types,
  aes(x = country, y = n, fill = category)
) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Landmark Composition by Country",
    subtitle = "Top 10 countries by classified landmark count",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Percentage of classified landmarks",
    fill = "Landmark type"
  )

print(p7)

# Interpretation:
# Each country's bar totals 100%.
# Segment sizes represent proportions, not absolute counts.


# ============================================================
# EDA 8: SCATTERPLOT AND SPEARMAN CORRELATION
# Question: Do landmarks with more Wikipedia language editions
# tend to receive more pageviews?
# ============================================================

popularity_data <- world_castles %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(sitelinks),
    !is.na(pageviews),
    sitelinks >= 0,
    pageviews >= 0
  )

p8 <- ggplot(
  popularity_data,
  aes(
    x = log10(sitelinks + 1),
    y = log10(pageviews + 1),
    color = category
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Wikipedia Language Coverage and Pageviews",
    subtitle = "Log transformations make large ranges easier to view",
    x = "log10(Language editions + 1)",
    y = "log10(Pageviews + 1)",
    color = "Landmark type"
  )

print(p8)

spearman_correlation <- cor(
  popularity_data$sitelinks,
  popularity_data$pageviews,
  method = "spearman"
)

print(spearman_correlation)

# Interpretation:
# A positive correlation suggests that greater language coverage
# tends to accompany more pageviews.
# Correlation does not establish causation.


# ============================================================
# EDA 8 EXTENSION: MANY LANGUAGE EDITIONS BUT FEW PAGEVIEWS
# ============================================================

# Exploratory definitions:
# "Many editions" = at or above the 75th percentile
# "Few pageviews" = at or below the 25th percentile

high_languages <- quantile(
  popularity_data$sitelinks, 0.75
)

low_views <- quantile(
  popularity_data$pageviews, 0.25
)

many_languages_few_views <- popularity_data %>%
  filter(
    sitelinks >= high_languages,
    pageviews <= low_views
  ) %>%
  select(name, country, category, sitelinks, pageviews) %>%
  arrange(desc(sitelinks), pageviews)

print(many_languages_few_views, n = 20)

# No matching rows is a valid result under these thresholds.


# ============================================================
# END OF EDA
# ============================================================
```
